Text:
# SUPPURATIVE INTRACRANIAL THROMBOPHLEBITIS

Adjust therapy from empirical regimens listed below after consultation with Infectious Disease or Neurosurgery services. Beta-lactam antibiotics are more effective than vancomycin against susceptible Staphylococci. If Staphylococcus is isolated, once methicillin-resistance is ruled out, switch to an anti-staphylococcal beta-lactam antibiotic. Pseudomonas is a potential pathogen in post-surgical patients or patients with known pseudomonas colonization.

# Consult Infectious Disease and Neurosurgery.

# Duration of Therapy

Treat for 3 to 6 weeks.

---

References:

- Kombogiorgas et al, British Journal of Neurosurgery, 2007, 21(6)603 - 609
- Mandell chapter: Subdural Empyema, Epidural Abscess, and Suppurative Intracranial Thrombophlebitis
Therapy:
Preferred if Pseudomonas is not suspected:

Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h ($) [M] <AND> metronidazole 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($)
[DI] <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

Preferred if Pseudomonas is suspected:

Cefepime 2gm IV q8h ($$) [R] <AND> metronidazole 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($)
[DI] <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

Alternative:

Assessment of beta-lactam reaction

Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h ($$) R,O  <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h ($) R

## Treatment if Methicillin-Sensitive S. Aureus is Isolated

Nafcillin 2 gm IV q4h ($$) R,DI

< OR >
Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h ($) R
